newsitem.title: USA: U.S. STOCKS END LOWER AS INTEREST RATE WOES MOUNT.
newsitem.headline: U.S. STOCKS END LOWER AS INTEREST RATE WOES MOUNT.

text.p: Wall Street stocks finished broadly lower on Thursday, as the weight of rising interest rates finally caught up to the high-flying equities market.

The Dow industrials skidded 71 points to end unofficially at 8188, reversing a 72 point blue chip rally on Wednesday. Broader indexes also fell and the Nasdaq composite saw its string of record closes snapped at six sessions.
Analysts pointed to a weak showing in the bond market as the catalyst for the decline. The yield on the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury rose four basis points to 6.52 percent.
"Yields went above 6.50 percent and that was a perfect excuse for some profit-taking in the market," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.

Analysts said a mixed market reception to the U.S. Treasury's auction of $10 billion in 30-year bonds touched off the weakness that sent rates rising. But they also noted heightened concern that the U.S. economy is picking up more steam than the Federal Reserve may be willing to tolerate.
New evidence of the economy's apparent resurgence came as retailers reported generally solid July sales figures today.
The sales figures may presage a strength in next week's national report on retail sales, considered to be a key element in the Fed's interest rate policy decision-making.

"That's absolutely going to be one of the more important pieces of data the Fed will look at," said Bill Meehan, market analyst at Prudential Securities. "So in that respect, today's figures might be a little bit of a cause for concern."

Among large retailers, Wal-Mart Stores Inc reported same-store sales rose 6.0 percent in July, in-line with forecasts. Increases at Kmart Corp and Federated Department Stores Inc were slightly above forecasts.
The good news met with a tame response from investors, however, with shares in Federated rising 5/16 to 43-9/16, while Kmart edged up 1/16 to 11-11/16 and Wal-Mart fell 5/16 to 38-1/16.
"A lot of the good news had already been fairly well discounted for the retailers," Meehan said. "Since the mid-April market lows, this group had been significantly outperforming the market."
Financial stocks ended sharply lower, hit hard by the rise in interest rates. Citicorp fell 3-3/8 to 136-1/2 and BankAmerica Corp shed 2-1/4 to 70-1/2.

In individual issues, Ethan Allen Interiors Inc jumped 6-15/16 to 61-11/16. Late Wednesday, the home furnishings company reported stronger than expected earnings and declared a two-for-one stock split.

United Healthcare Corp tumbled 7-5/16 to 50-3/4 after the health maintenance organization reported weaker than expected second quarter earnings, two days after another HMO company, Aetna Inc reported disappointing results.
Shares in Aetna extended their recent slide, falling 5-1/4 to 96-3/4.

Pioneer Hi-Bred International Inc surged 13-7/16 to 90 after the seed and agricultural biotechnology company said it reached a deal to sell a $1.7 billion equity stake to DuPont Co. Shares in DuPont rose 1/4 to 69.
The S&P 500 index fell 9.13 points to 951.19.
The Nasdaq Composite index fell 6.26 points to 1624.18.
